These "miracle children" embody the tragedy of the camp, described by the U.N. A 15-year-old girl was detained at Cape Town International Airport in South Africa after authorities received information she was attempting to leave the country to join ISIS. State Security Minister David Mahlobo stated the girl had been radicalized on social media platforms, and police and airport security intercepted her on a Johannesburg-bound flight, subsequently debriefing her family and releasing her into their care. The incident highlights the growing global concern of recruiting and radicalizing young people to commit acts of terror.

The outburst occurred as he faces first-degree charges for the killing of Ron Lane at Wayne Community College, with investigators probing whether it was a hate crime due to the victim's sexuality. In Garissa, Kenya, the Madrassa school where the suspected attack mastermind once taught sits empty as students mourn three national deaths following a deadly university attack. The authorities link Mohamed Mohamud, a former Madrassa teacher now based in Al-Shabaab, to the massacre, fueling concern that porous border-based militants are recruiting local youth. Sheikh Khalif Abdi Hussein, principal, insists the school is unrelated to Mohamud's violent ideas as Kenya graples with its deadliest attack since 1998.

Pope Francis commemorated the 100th anniversary of the Armenian genocide by referencing Pope John Paul II's 2001 statement, marking a significant shift in Vatican diplomacy. This deliberate use of the term "genocide" underscores the Church's commitment to historical continuity while navigating complex geopolitical sensitivities regarding Turkey.

The NFL suspended Peterson in November over allegations of child abuse, but a district court judge vacated the decision upholding his suspension in February, making him eligible to play. Peterson is considered one of the best running backs in the NFL and the Vikings issued a statement saying they "look forward to Adrian rejoining the team."

A Tulsa County reserve deputy mistakenly shot and killed a suspect during an arrest at a Dollar General parking lot, believing he was using his Taser instead of his service weapon. The deputy, Robert Bates, was placed on administrative leave as the investigation into the death of Eric Harris continues.

Chinese police arrested over 133,000 people and seized 43.3 tons of narcotics during a six-month anti-drug campaign. The operation also handled 115,000 drug-related crimes and 606,000 cases of drug use, representing nearly double the figures from the same period a year earlier. However, the crackdown resulted in the deaths of nine police officers and 657 injuries, while authorities intensified online drug trafficking crackdowns following the arrest of entertainment figures like Jaycee Chan.

Jack White announced a hiatus from touring to focus on an unprecedented acoustic quartet. The limited tour will cover only five remaining U.S. states, with shows announced only on the day of performance and tickets sold on a first-come basis at $3 each.

CNN reports that UNICEF has been granted rare access to land in Sanaa Airport on a desperate aid mission. Despite the airport being previously bombed and a likely imminent resumption of hostilities, a brief, negotiated ceasefire allows for the delivery of vital food and supplies to ease Yemen's worsening humanitarian crisis. With over 100,000 civilians fled and 15.9 million in need of assistance, UNICEF and other NGOs remain the only hope for those with nowhere to go and no chance of an evacuation flight out.

Tomasz Lazar's photography project captures the haunting faces of Poles deported to Siberia as children during World War II, documenting their traumatic experiences to preserve their stories for future generations. The portraits, taken seven decades later, reveal the deep wrinkles and haunted eyes of survivors in their 80s, who finally shared their stories after the fall of the Soviet Union. Lazar's work serves as a vital reminder "not to make the same mistakes."

His lawyer, Scott Wood, claims the records show Bates completed the necessary training, though the Tulsa County Sheriff's Office has denied allegations that supervisors were told to forge his records. The documents are central to the case, as the family of Harris claims Bates wasn't qualified and received preferential treatment due to donations and personal relationships.

Hernandez confessed to police three years ago, but his lawyer argues he is mentally ill and unable to discern if he committed the crime. A judge previously ruled Hernandez's confession and waiver of Miranda rights were legal, allowing it as evidence. The case has remained prominent due to the Patz family's efforts to keep it alive and create awareness of missing children.

ABC is developing a revival of "The Muppets," with "Big Bang Theory" co-creator Bill Prady co-writing the pilot. The presentation is set to film at the Disney lot in Burbank, featuring original performers and the regular cast of characters. However, the project won't move forward unless Miss Piggy signs on, as her current relationship with Kermit is on the rocks. If ABC orders it to series, Prady would juggle the project with his work on CBS' "Big Bang Theory."

Twenty-five years later, she continues to hear similar stories of women and girls facing harassment on public transport and in daily life, realizing that her childhood trauma likely caused her adult phobia of trains; despite pervasive societal silence and underreporting, she has spent two years encouraging women to share their experiences and reclaim their power to confront harassment.

Canadian actor Jonathan Crombie, best known for playing Gilbert Blythe in the "Anne of Green Gables" TV movies, has died at age 48. He passed away from complications of a brain hemorrhage, leaving behind a legacy as a cultural touchstone for fans who grew up with the series. Crombie's portrayal of the character, opposite to Megan Follows, became a heartthrob for many, with one fan tweeting he was the crush of a generation.

Al-Shabaab's latest attack on Garissa University College, killing 147, marks the deadliest assault in Kenya over the past year and a half, eclipsing their 2013 Westgate Mall siege. The group, degraded by African Union forces and U.S. drone strikes, increasingly targets soft civilian sites rather than military bases, highlighting their weakening as they lose ground in Somalia.

Former rap mogur Marion "Suge" Knight was ordered to stand trial for murder and other charges stemming from a deadly hit-and-run on the movie set of "Straight Outta Compton." The judge reduced Knight's bail from $25 million to $10 million and dismissed one hit-and-run count, meaning he will face trial on one count of murder, attempted murder, and one count of hit-and-run. Knight, 49, could life in prison if convicted, and his fiancee Toi Kelly reported he is "doing much better" following the hearing.

National Park Week, running from April 18 to 26, offers free admission to the 128 fee-charging U.S. national parks, including Yosemite and Yellowstone, to encourage public exploration. The National Park Service and the National Park Foundation are coordinating the event, which features astronomy parties, Revolutionary War programs, and Junior Ranger activities, and encourages visitors to share their experiences via #FindYourPark.

CNN reports on the affordable housing crisis in Silicon Valley, highlighting families like Nicole, a single mother living in a garage, and alongside 16 people in one home. With 7.7 million low-income households spending over half their income on rent nationally, HUD advocates swift action to preserve existing housing and prevent further displacement.

An American citizen was shot multiple times while driving from a medical school in Karachi, Pakistan, on Thursday. Debra Lobo, a 55-year-old California native, was struck in the right cheek and left arm but is expected to survive. Police believe the assainants, who fled on a motorcycle and threw pamphlets reading "America should be burnt," targeted her.

Jarret Stoll of the L.A. Kings was arrested at a Las Vegas resort pool on drug-possession charges involving cocaine and ecstasy. He was released on $5,000 bail as the Kings conducted an internal investigation. The incident comes as the team, who did not make the playoffs this season, faces off-IHL with TV personality Erin Andrews.

A Walmart clerk gave the suspect ammunition after he claimed he would break the case, and he subsequently fired into the air before an officer struck him with a patrol car, ending the spree. The government condemned the violence while praising police for preventing further bloodshed, noting the attacks are not representative of the broader public support for refugees.

Growing fears suggest Saudi Arabia and Iran are fighting a proxy war for regional domination, resulting in hundreds of casualties while the U.N. Security Council enforces an arms embargo on the Houthis.

The Chilean government estimates that around 2 million people will be able to benefit from the change.

The next time you fly to see Grandma in Florida, look down. If you take the kids to see the talking mouse, or go to South Beach for some sun, get a window seat and spend the moments before landing contemplating the seemingly endless swamp below. Because there are few places that represent the folly of man -- and the cost of redemption -- like the Everglades. On approach into Miami or Orlando, it just looks like squishy wasteland full of things that want to hurt you: snakes and scorpions, rats and roaches, gators and mosquitoes. (A researcher once caught 365,000 bloodthirsty bugs in a single trap in a single night.)

CNN reports that ISIS militants took control of Yarmouk, a Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus, after defeating local militia groups. Syrian forces had bombed and besieged the area for over two years. Residents describe the takeover as terrifying, saying militants "slaughtered" people in the streets. The group now controls almost all of the camp.

China has long used a "Great Firewall" to block its citizens from reading critical articles or accessing content it disapproves of. But a new study says they have crossed that border. They have developed a new weapon called the "Great Cannon," which attacks servers outside China's borders, including in the United States. The study's authors say that going on the attack so visibly and handily within another country's borders will probably draw international ire, and Beijing may have counted on that.

A German official said the investigation into the Germanwings Flight 9525 crash has not found a clear reason for the co-pilot's actions. However, the official said the pilot, Andreas Lubitz, had suicidal thoughts before he became a pilot. He received medical treatment and therapy for these thoughts. Investigators have not found any writings or conversations explaining his motives.

The leader of Yemen's Houthi rebels said on Sunday that they will not give back. A top Saudi military official said that weeks of airst strikes had hurt the Shiite group. The rebel leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi said on TV that his fighters will not leave the main cities or the government institutions. He said that anyone who thinks they will surrender is dreaming. His comments came after more than three weeks of Saudi-led coalition bombings. The Houriz surged into the capital of Sanaa in January and ousted President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power.

Twenty years ago, on April 19, 1995, Timothy McVeigh drove a truck filled with a massive bomb into the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The explosion killed 168 people and injured many others. It is the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in U.H. history.

The attack shocked the country. It wasn't just the scale of the tragedy that drew attention, but the fact that American citizens were targeting their own government with deadly force for the first time.

If you care deeply about something, would you protest? Make a sign? Join a demonstration? How long could you keep going for, in the face of indifference and inaction?

When more than 200 Nigerian girls were kidnapped from their school a year ago by Boko Haram militants, millions of people around the world joined a social media campaign to plead for their safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of those people -- from celebrities to world leaders -- voicing their anger via #BringBackOurGirls, one of the top Twitter hashtags of 2014, used in more than four million tweets. But as weeks turned into months, there was still no sign of the missing girls. The spotlight on the campaign faded.

CNN reports that Barney Frank, a retired congressman, is very experienced in politics. He recently spoke at a full-packed event in Chicago, entertaining a crowd at the Center on Halsted by detailing his 45 years of public service. Frank is known as the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same-sex while in office. He also had strong words for closeted politicians who vote against LGBT rights. When asked about a current ballot proposal in California that would legalize killing gay people, he said he was not aware of the measure but told the young man not to worry about "c crazy people."

A brutal attack at Garissa University College in Kenya has left nearly 150 people dead, including students, and dozens more wounded. Gunmen attacked the campus early Thursday while morning prayers were happening, shooting indiscriminately and taking hostages before being killed by security forces. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi said Al-Shabaab militants have claimed responsibility. The attack comes just months after Al-Shabaab militants murdered non-Muslim workers in a Kenyan quarry. The terrorist group has been behind numerous attacks in the region. It has also recruited some Americans, particularly from the Somali-American community in Minnesota.

A South African university is taking down a statue of a British colonialist after weeks of protests. Students at the University of Cape Town used social media to demand the statue of Cecil Rhodes come down, saying his legacy is tainted with racism. Using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall, students started a campaign last month. Four weeks later, the hashtag is now #RhodesHas Fallen. The university said Wednesday the heritage authority granted it permission to remove the statue from the campus. "These steps are being taken to ensure the safety of the statue while matters concerning its future are resolved," the university said in a statement.

Syria is a very dangerous place. An group fighting the government says the number of people who have died has doubled in the last year. Since the civil war started, 310,000 people have been killed. A year earlier, the number was 162,402. And a year before that, the United Nations said 70,000 people had died. The United Nations also says that violence has pushed more than half of all Syrians into such bad poverty that they are in dire need of survival aid, as food rations are being cut for lack of donations.

CNN reports that Ailina Tsarnaeva went into Manhattan Criminal Court quietly. Prosecutors say she threatened a woman on the phone this summer, telling her to "Leave my man alone" and warning, "I know people that can put a bomb where you live." Because of who she is, prosecutors did not see the threat as a joke. They charged her with aggravated harassment, a charge she denies. Tsarnaeva is the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev.

CNN reports that a door with a drawing by the artist Banksy was taken by police in Gaza on Thursday. The owner, Rabea Darduna, said he sold the door for only $175 because he did not know how it was valuable. The door is now with the Khan Younis police in southern Gaza until a court hearing. When Darduna's home was destroyed last summer's war, he says he felt he was left with nothing. Only a doorway and a door.

A Saudi-led coalition is attacking Houthi rebels in Yemen. Five days after they started airstrikes, the coalition has destroyed most of Yemen's air defenses and air bases. Saudi Arabia has stopped all Yemeni ports, only allowing inited medical aid to enter. Locals are fleeing the fighting, and many civilians have been killed.

Holland manager Guus Hiddink was very angry about his own fans booing Spain player Andres Iniesta. He called them a "disgrace". Spain coach Vicente del Bosque made an experimental side, and Iniesta came in the 76th minute to the sound of booing. Goals from Stefan de Vrij and Davy Klaassen gave Holland a 2-0 victory.

Scotland will find out on May 21 if their Euro 2016 qualifier with Georgia is played behind closed doors. UEFA has started disciplinary proceedings against the Georgian Football Federation after fans twice invaded the field during Sunday's 2-0 defeat by Germany in Tbilisi. European football's governing body is also set to look at charges that allege home fans were guilty of setting off fireworks while a string of safety breaches, including blocked stairs, locked gates and a lack of body searches by staff at the Boris Paichadze Stadium, will also be investigated. A fan invades the pitch during Georgia's 2-0 defeat by Germany on Sunday in Tbilisi.

Football agents were left waiting on Wednesday after learning about new rules. Starting April 1st, anyone can become a football agent by paying £500 for a one-year registration. The FA will then charge £250 every year to renew the license. Those already licensed are exempt from these changes. The FA was supposed to put a link on their website for agents to register, but as of 1pm that was still not there. Mel Stein thinks the new rules will 'create anarchy'. The new rules came in after FIFA effectively gave up governing agents.

Maksims Uvarenko, the Latvian goalkeeper for CSKA Sofia, has not been paid for three months. He has had to ask his parents for money to pay his rent. Despite this financial problem, Uvarenko has been impressed by the fans' passionate support since joining the club in January.

He told local media that the lack of money is the biggest problem he has faced at CSKA. He has not received any salary since joining the club three months ago.

David Moore, 25, got angry on the road after leaving his home and immediately got stuck in heavy traffic with Rafal Cegielka, 45, who was picking up his child from St John's Primary School in Burnley, Lancashire. A father was punched and had his car smashed with a hockey stick in front of his children because Moore was having a "bad day" and "saw red."

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday. The loss reminded people of Spain's poor showing in the 2014 World Cup. Coach Vicente del Bosque is not worried, says Gerard Pique. Holland beat Spain 5-1 in the group stage last year, ending Spain's six-year time as the best team. Holland scored two early goals at the Amsterdam Arena and held on against Spain pressure in the second half for the 2-0 win.

A New York City mother and named Ulrike Berger ran to Germany with her daughter during a custody battle, police claim. Ulrike Berger, 44, is barred by a court order from leaving the country with seven-year-old Kaia. But on March 22, a day after the little girl was dropped off for a weekend visit, they are believed to have boarded a plane to Europe. Manhunt: Police are searching for Ulrike Berger, 44, (left) and her seven-year-old daughter Kaia (right). It is believed the pair boarded a plane from New York to Germany on March 22, violating a custody court order . Police say the pair were last seen at Berger's home in Boerun Hill, Brooklyn, at 10

Strong winds and dry weather caused a massive wildfire near the south coast. The fire started deliberately and burned about 70 hectares of heathland. The area was very dry because it was on a hill, and water had run off the slope. The fire came after recent storms that had felled trees and shut roads. In total, three separate areas—half a hectare, one hectare, and 70 hectares—were destroyed.

Last night, emergency services were overwhelmed with 600 calls an hour as people across Britain celebrated the 2012 New Year. Ammed stretchers were pushed to the limit, and in Cambridge a Territorial Army field hospital was set up to treat inebebebeb partygoers. The London Ambulance Service said at the peak they were dealing with over 600 calls per hour, which is more than three times as many as on a normal night.

In Manchester, a man collapsed on the pavement next to an ambulance as two revellers walk past eating a late night takeaway. In Manchester, a man is stood slumped over in a doorway as two women walk by as they celebrate the New Year.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet says his mental strength helped him recover after being dropped in December. Mignolet was left out of the team indefinitely after a poor run of form, but he returned quickly when Brad Jones got a thigh injury. The 27-year-old Belgian told he remained upbeat despite the disappointment.

Simon Mignolet has revealed how his mental strength helped him recover after being dropped . Mignolet (second right) makes a save from a free kick during a league match against Swansea last month . Mignolet told FourFourTwo: 'I was positive.

Giant hailstones the size of plums crashed down over the South on Tuesday with residents rushing out to capture the freak weather. Twitter user Arke USA from Bryant, Arkansas, filmed the ice balls peppering his backyard and noisily plopping into the swimming pool. Footage shows the hailstones coming down at speed, with many cracking as they hit the ground. Despite it being around 80-degrees, the compacted lumps prove resilient to the heat taking a good while to melt. In a matter of seconds the patio is completely covered in snow-white pellets.

Here is the rewritten version in plain, simple English:

Huge hailstones the size of plums crashed down over the South on Tuesday. People ran outside to take pictures of the strange weather

A replica pirate ship ran into trouble about 30 miles off the coast of Maine. The crew of the Liana's Ransom had to abandon their vessel after the engines failed in rough seas. Nine people were rescued by Coast Guard life boats on Tuesday. The ship was left adrift after the sails became wrapped around the mast. The crew had to leap from the ship to get to the rescue boats.

Amazing pictures have emerged of blue fluorescent algae lighting up Australia's east coast. The images were taken in Jervis Bay, the south coast of NSW, as the neon glow illuminated one of Australia's popular beaches. Photographer Andy Hutchinson described the sight as a 'beautiful supernatural scene' caused by millions of plankton omitting light. A similar display was shown in Sydney's Manly Beach back in August 2014 where an oceanography expert told Daily Mail Australia there was no need to be concerned about the algae.

A teenage boy named Rahul Kumar, 17, climbed into a lions' enclosure at a zoo in Ahmedabad. He was drunk and high. He started running towards the animals and shouted that he would kill them. Zoo security rescued him.

A 12-year-old boy fell out of a five-story window and survived by landing on a car parked beneath the building. According to his father, the boy most likely fell while sleepwalking. The incident happened last Saturday in Nanchang, the provincial capital of Jiangxi in southeastern China, reported the People’s Daily Online. A hotel receptionist working across the road said she heard a loud bang around midnight, which she thought was a car accident.

Red Wings player Drew Miller is happy to be back on the ice just one day after getting a bad cut to his face. He said on Wednesday that he feels lucky the skate didn't hit his eye. He had a bad wound on his face that needed many stitches to close. He was left with a scar across his eye, but he did not lose any eyesight.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends. Atletico Madrid wants to bring him back in the summer. The full back signed a three-year deal last July but has struggled to play left back at Stamford Bridge. Atletico hope this may give them leverage, but Luis said: ‘I’m happy at Chelsea. I want to stay at the club until the end of my contract.’

A Reading fan named Charlie Sumner got a three-year ban from football after running onto the pitch at Madejski Stadium. Sumner, who was 20 years old, did this during a FA Cup game last month. His team was winning 3-0 against Bradford City when he ran onto the field. He performed four front flips, landing on his back, before stewards caught him. Sumner said going to his first game was a 'brilliant experience'.

A video shows a group of men riding on top of a van. The van swed around a corner and toppled onto one side at high speed. About half a dozen people were sitting on the roof of the vehicle on a road near the coastal city of Salé, Morocco. Terrifying footage was taken from a car following the van, which was understood to have been transporting football fans.

England have been drawn in Group D with the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy at the UEFA Under 17 European Championships in Bulgaria this May.

John Peacock's Young Lions are the defending champions after defeating Holland on penalties in last year's final in Malta.

To advance to the quarter-finals, England will have to overcome the Dutch again.

This tournament has been expanded from eight to 16 nations for the first time.

An annoyed elephant tried to spray a bull with water because it got too close. The elephant was relaxing in South Africa with its family by a small pool when the bull approached. In a video, the elephant squits water from its trunk to chase the bull away, but misses. The frustrated elephant tries to spray the bull again, which has wandered too close. Its young elephant coses up to its parent for protection, as the bull drinks from a small pool of water.

Michael Thorpe, a former pub landlord, has had his conviction overturned after an eight-year legal fight. He was convicted in 2006 for showing a Premier League game on foreign TV at his pub in Plymouth. The court has cleared his name, but he has lost his pub and paid a heavy price to clear his name.

The Irish Football Association is worried that damage at their home in Belfast might stop the team's important game against Romania in June. Cracks were found in the West Stand on Tuesday morning, and engineers checked the damage. The association found out on Tuesday morning that overnight damage had been caused to the West Stand of the National Football Stadium at Windsor Park. Northern Ireland's Windsor Park suffered overnight damage to its West Stand on Monday night.

A 20-year-old football fan ran onto the pitch during his first ever game at the stadium. He was topless and did four front flips. The fan, Charlie Sumner, did this during Reading's game at Madejski Stadium. He was three years banned for this.

A BMW driver with five children was arrested after a student was killed while walking to the library. Hina Shamim, 21, died near the University of Kingston in London. She was weeks away from her 22nd birthday. Friends left flowers and said she was a much-loved, charming girl from Peterborough. She was killed walking near her home.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested after a video of them fighting with a student at a high school was posted online. The pair were caught on camera at Langham Creek High School in Houston on Tuesday. The mother was reportedly angry with the girl because she had allegedly been bullying her daughter. In the video, the mother is seen in a black top on the right and the victim is center wearing white.

The chief executive of Stoke, Tony Scholes, hopes they can keep their goalkeeper, Asmir Begovic, who is in the final year of his contract. Begovic, the Bosnia international, has been linked with other clubs. Although his current deal has just over 12 months left, Scholes believes they can match the 27-year-old's ambitions. 'Clearly Asmir is a terrific goalkeeper and we are very keen to keep him at the club,' he told The Sentinel. 'I think when you've got extremely good players it is only natural that there will be speculation about their future.'

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand was filmed by a passenger while reading a newspaper. The driver was seen flicking through the pages while the bus was moving. When the bus stopped at traffic lights, he moved his head to read a page. His boss, Andrew Ritchie, called him a "complete idiot" and said he was embarrassed by his actions.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says Winston Reid will play Saturday against Leicester City. Reid injured his hamstring in March but is now fit. Enner Valencia will not play. He missed the last two games because of a toe injury. Allardyce says Valencia is not match fit.

Five days before their wedding last May, Brittany Huber and John Redman were in a bad car crash on a Georgia highway. Brittany died, and Redman was badly hurt. Doctors said he would likely spend the rest of his life in a nursing home, stuck in a wheelchair. The future looked dark for the 25-year-old coach at Dalton State College, but Redman recovered against all odds. On March 24, he helped lead his team to a championship.

Lucas (left) and Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard during Sunday's All-Star charity game at Anfield. Liverpool midfielder Lucas Leiva is trying to get back to his best form after returning from injury. The Brazil international played 16 games in 19 matches from late November to mid-December. During that time, the team's results improved. In February, he missed 10 games because of a groin problem. He was an unused substitute in the defeat by Manchester United immediately before the international break, their first in the league since mid-December, but played 90 minutes in Sunday's All-Star Charity game at Anfield.

Sick of awkward father-daughter photos? One photographer, Yûki Aoyama, found a funny way to make them better. The series shows teenage girls looking at the camera and smiling, while their fathers pose dramatically in the air next to them. These photos are from Aoyama's latest book, which roughly translates as "Daughter and Salary Man."

Police are looking for a man between 50 and 60 years old. He is suspected of robbing a bank in broad daylight and running off with £3,000 in cash.

The robbery happened at 12:30pm at a Lloyds Bank branch in Fairwater, Cardiff. Detectives have released CCTV images of the suspect. He is between 5ft 9in and 6ft, was wearing black clothing, and has greying black hair and glasses.

The white male suspect was captured on camera inside the bank. Detectives said no one was injured during the robbery and they were confident the public would be able to identify the suspect.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has lifted Morocco's ban from the next two editions of the African Cup of Nations. The ban was originally imposed by the Confederation of African Football. Morocco was expelled from the 2017 and 2019 tournaments and was fined $1 million by the CAF. The CAF also demanded a further $9 million in compensation, after the country pulled out because of fears related to the Ebola epidemic. Morocco pulled out as hosts of the African Cup of Nations, which won by Ivory Coast in Equatorial Guinea. Morocco can now compete in the next two African Cup of Nations after the initial ban was imposed.

Tom Boyd says Jason Denayer’s successful loan at Celtic means he is ready to challenge for a spot at Manchester City next season. Giving Denayer another year at Celtic was Ronny Deila’s plan, but Boyd thinks Denayer moving to City is a positive. He believes Denayer’s success will encourage other young players to join at Celtic. The 19-year-old defender recently earned his first cap for Belgium in a Euro 2016 qualifier against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend scored a great goal for England, silencing his critics. People like Paul Merson had motivated him while playing in Italy. This has been an up-and-down season for the 23-year-old, who has not yet played as well as he did when he first started on the international scene. England manager Roy Hodgson has kept faith with Tottenham winger Townsend, and Townsend paid the manager back in an exceptional way at Juventus Stadium. On Tuesday night, Townsend scored England's equaliser in their 1-1 friendly draw with Italy in Turin. Townsend celebrates his strike with Tottenham Hotspur team-mates Ryan Mason (left) and Kyle Walker .

Chinese company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought 20 percent of Spanish soccer team Atletico Madrid. The purchase was finalized at a special meeting on Tuesday. The legal team representing Wanda Madrid Investment signed off on buying 726,707 shares for €45 million (£32.8 million). The deal was first announced in January, but two special meetings were needed to finalize it. Wanda Group chairman Wang Jianlin hopes to grow Atletico's brand in Asia. Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone speaks to the media.

Antonio Conte returned to Turin for Italy's 1-1 draw against England. He said the trip brought up "very fond memories," despite reports that he received death threats in the days before the friendly.

 Conte replaced Cesare Prandelli as Italy boss in August after the team's World Cup group-stage exit last summer. His first seven months in charge have been very unstable. Italy needed a late goal from Eder to rescue a 2-2 draw against Bulgaria last Saturday. Conte reportedly received death threats from Juventus fans after Claudio Marchisio suffered a knee injury on the eve of the Euro 2016 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that Hibs can catch Rangers for second spot. His Dumbarton team have played both sides already this season and will again at the end. But while Rangers are winning now - beating Hibs and Cowdenbeath - Murray would not be surprised if the power swings back to Easter Road soon. He believes Rangers will struggle to keep their pace.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet returned to England after playing for Belgium in World Cup qualifying games. Although he was named in the match-day squad, he did not play. Backup goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois started instead. Mignolet shared pictures of him posing in an airplane cockpit on Facebook on Wednesday.

A large rural estate is for sale for £6 million. The property, called Chyknell Hall Estate, is near Bridgnorth in Shropshire. It has a Grade II-listed manor house from 1814 and five cottages. The house has 11 bedrooms, a swimming pool, a tennis court, and stables. It also has its own cricket green. The large grounds are secluded and private. The house has only had two different owners since it was built.

Two college campus police officers in Dallas have been placed on leave after a student filmed them harassing and arresting a group of four students. The incident happened at El Centro College last Wednesday. Student Charles Adams filmed the video while smoking a cigarette. The officers approached the students while they waited for a bus outside the downtown campus.

Kilmarnock has made Gary Locke their permanent manager. The 39-year-old, who was the assistant boss before, took the job in February after Allan Johnston left. He has only lost one game in seven since taking charge. Locke signed a three-year deal and shook hands with chairman Jim Mann.

This weekend, one of the biggest games on the German football schedule takes place. Usually called "Der Klassiker," this match pits Borussia Dortmund against Bayern Munich. These two teams have shared the last five league titles. Bayern are set to keep their domestic dominance this term.

This time, the two great foys of German football meet with 31 points and nine positions separating them in the standings. However, this does not mean the stakes are not as high as they always are when these two clubs meet. Jurgen Klop (centre) celebrates with his Borussia Dortmund players after their victory against Hannover.

A 14-year-old girl was left stranded at a busy airport. She was not allowed to board her easyJet flight home to Spain because she had two pieces of hand luggage. Deva Joseph was upset and crying at London Stansted airport. She offered to pay for the second bag to be put in the hold, but was told only credit cards would be accepted. She is too young to have a credit card.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed John Potts, 45, with a single punch to the back of the head. The force of the blow caused an audible crack, and Mr. Potts fell down dead. Robson had been drunk after his grandfather's funeral when he stepped in to break up a fight outside a sports bar. Newcastle Crown Court heard that Robson, who has a history of violent offending, was jailed for three and a half years for the attack outside the NE38 Sports Bar in Washington, Tyne and Wear, in November last year.
Ellen White scored a free kick against her old team, Notts County. She scored while her teammate Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood ran into each other by the ball. This happened in the 26th minute.

These are the amazing scenes as high school girls in China are put through their paces with military-style dagger drills. Each of the girls shout the words 'kill, stab, slash and jab' as they perform each of the eight set movements involved in the high-intensity knife-fighting session. According to the People's Daily Online, the girls of the 27th March Huizhou Integrated High School are being trained by former special forces solider Inspector Tan. The 68 girls involved in the training are all aged between 16 and 18, however in a concession to safety, the knives are not real. School official Huang Anruo said: 'The daggers are fake.

We spend about one-third of our lives sleeping. However, most people do not realize what their mind and body actually need during these resting hours in order to feel refreshed every day. According to the Sleep Health Foundation, a new study reports that 30 percent of Australians complain about their lack of sleep on a daily basis. According to Chair Professor David Hillman, those misplaced hours of sleep must be "paid back" in order to be functional for the entire week. A study has outlined that 30 percent of Australians complain about their lack of sleep on a daily basis. The average adult needs around eight hours of sleep per night, with a range of seven to nine.

A video posted on Facebook shows a heated argument between neighbours in a Perth suburb. The argument escalated into a physical confrontation where a woman brandished a crowbar and shouted racial slurs at a group of men. The men fought back, and a scrawl ensued.

Everyone is watching 19-year-old Valencia left back Jose Luis Gaya. Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea want to sign him from Real Madrid this summer. Sportsmail writer Pete Jenson looks at the Spain under 21 defender. Why are English clubs so keen? His buy-out clause is £13.5m. When you consider that Luke Shaw – of a similar age and potential – cost £27m it would be silly not to be interested; although there would be also be reservations about his suitability to the Premier League. Jose Luis Gaya (right) in action for Valencia during a La Liga match with Sevilla earlier this season .

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help finding a motorcyclist who stopped a man from threatening two teens with a gun. The man, Edward West, 59, allegedly pointed a gun at the teens and told them "get ready to die." A stranger on a green motorcycle stepped in and used his helmet to knock the gun out of the man's hands, letting the teens escape.

Tim Sherwood wants Ron Vlaar to play well to help Aston Villa avoid relegation. Sherwood reminded Vlaar that people might have forgotten his good play at the World Cup last year. Vlaar was a key player for Holland when they reached the semi finals in Brazil. He missed a penalty in a shoot-out against Argentina. Because of this, he got linked with Manchester United. Now, Vlaar is fit and returns to help Villa in their battle against relegation.

Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about a possible takeover of Aston Villa this summer. He plans to build a team for next season if the club stays up. Randy Lerner is in talks with a possible buyer. If a new owner takes over, questions about Sherwood's job might come up. But Sherwood is focused on keeping Villa up, and then plans to make changes in the closed season. Christian Benteke scored as Villa thundered Sunderland last month.

Celtic hoped to keep Jason Denyer on loan from Manchester City next season. However, City's manager Pepi Guardiola says his young players are not ready for the first team. So, Denyer might have to return to City to fill a gap. Denyer has done well while playing for Celtic this season.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting for a more accurate date on Fraser Forster's return before deciding if he needs to sign another goalkeeper in the summer. Forster had knee surgery after falling awkwardly in the 2-0 victory over Burnley a fortnight ago. Estimates for his comeback have ranged from four to 12 months. Koeman is reluctant to give a more precise time frame and views Kelvin Davis as a capable deputy, although he admits he may be forced to bolster his goalkeeping options if Forster's recovery is delayed. Fraser Forster suffered a serious knee injury in Southampton's match with Burnley a couple of weeks ago.

Rotherham manager Steve Evans was angry on the sidelines after his team, which is in danger of being relegated, was denied a penalty in their Championship loss at Birmingham. Birmingham had scored first through Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson. Matt Derbyshire pulled one back for Rotherham, who are in fourth position. However, Rob Kiernan clumsily handled Derbyshire near the hour mark, and the former City forward went down in the box. Only for referee Dean Whitestone to wave away appeals for a spot-kick, leaving the Millers boss visibly enraged as the home side held out. Robert Tesche of Birmingham City celebrates scoring the opening goal of the game.

The worry about Virgil van Dijk is clear to see. Holland’s national team has already let more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifiers than they gave up in the whole qualifying campaign for the last World Cup. And still, Guus Hiddink never calls or writes. The Celtic defender made it into two squads last year. But one step forward is usually followed by two steps back. When the Dutch were drawing 1-1 with Turkey the other night he was sunning himself in the Arabian Gulf and bumping into club-mates instead. Virgil van Dijk has been in fine form for Celtic but wasn't rewarded with a call-up to the Holland national team.

Celtic have complained to the SFA about ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final at Hampden this month. The game is being played at 12.15pm on Sunday, April 18 - before the first trains from Inverness arrive in Glasgow. The SFA has already come under fire from Caley Thistle fans for scheduling the match. Now the Parkhead club have made their feeling known after ticket prices were set at £23 for the North and South stands, with the East Stand being £15 for adults and £5 for concessions.

Rangers interim chairman Paul Murray says the club was forced to leave the stock market because of the previous board's mistakes. The team will be forced to delist from the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) after being unable to secure a new nominated advisor (Nomad) to meet regulations. Murray insists the new board’s plans for the future will be unaffected and that planned investments will still take place.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were upset about how they started against Italy on Tuesday night. Nine months after they met at the World Cup, the Three Lions faced the Azzurri again in a friendly match at the Juventus Stadium. Hopes were high after seven straight wins, but Roy Hodgson's men struggled in the first half, falling behind to a Graziano Pelle header in Turin.

England captain Wayne Rooney gave instructions during the 1-1 draw against Italy on Tuesday night. Rooney said he and the rest of the England players were upset by their first half performance.
